question.problem:
$\,$ $5$ is prime and $\{5\}$ is not empty.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
question.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(5\text{ is prime}\text{ and }\{5\}\text{ is not empty}) & ≡¬((5\text{ is prime})∧(\{5\}\text{ is not empty})) \\  & ≡¬(5\text{ is prime})∨¬(\{5\}\text{ is not empty}) \\  & ≡(5\text{ is not prime})∨(\{5\}\text{ is empty}) \\  & ≡5\text{ is not prime}\text{ or }\{5\}\text{ is empty}.\end{aligned}
$$
